gate_1_sharp_test_tn36_row1_detected.principle: tn36's engines model row 1 and nothing else, so row 1 is the band whose masking decides whether the six perfect-1.0 candidates stay perfect. A detector that cannot see it cannot fix the metric. NOTE this gate is about DETECTION only -- gate 4 is what decides whether it may be used.

gate_2_every_stage1_accepted_band_carrie.principle: changed_fraction alone cannot distinguish a counter row from the row the player walks along, so 'the detector flagged it' is not by itself a licence to delete cells. Every accepted band passed at least one decoupling discriminator.

gate_3_no_stage1_accepted_band_tripped_a.principle: over-masking destroys CORRECTNESS while under-masking only costs efficiency (logical_hud_mask's own docstring), so any alarm on either corpus excludes the band.

gate_4_every_shipped_mask_is_clean_on_BO.principle: REQ-ARC-WMTE-6017: a verdict is a statement about (mask, corpus), never about the mask alone. A mask cleared only on the corpus it was derived from is not cleared.

gate_5_documented_over_masking_table_rep.principle: If this audit could not reproduce the two over-masking cases the project already knows about, its clean verdicts on the other games would carry no weight. Reproducing them to four decimals is what makes the accepts meaningful.

gate_6_detector_thresholds_untouched.principle: detect_hud_registers was called with its shipped defaults on all 20 games, and the audit can only ever REMOVE a band. Hand-tuning a threshold until a game came out the way the hypothesis wanted would make the capture unfalsifiable -- and tn36, the game the hypothesis most wanted, is the one that got withheld.

gate_7_capture_is_repeatable.principle: Two full independent runs must detect the same bands, or the masks are not re-derivable by anyone else and the audit is unauditable.

A_DEFECT_THE_REVIEW_DID_NOT_FIND_alarm_A.how_to_fix_it_in_the_next_capture: report A1 as a three-valued signal (clean / alarm / unavailable-no-clicks) rather than a bool, the same way P1 and P2 already report `available`.
A_DEFECT_THE_REVIEW_DID_NOT_FIND_alarm_A.what: Alarm A1 asks whether the winning route ever CLICKS inside the band. On three of the six masked games the route contains no click actions at all -- ar25 (0 clicks, 15 mover-centroid actions), ls20 (0 clicks, 13), tu93 (0 clicks, 18) -- so A1 could not have fired on those games no matter what the band was.
A_DEFECT_THE_REVIEW_DID_NOT_FIND_alarm_A.why_it_matters: a test that cannot fail is not evidence, and the capture reported A1's silence identically on all six games. Three of the six A1 'passes' carry no information. This does not change any decision -- every band has at least two other legs, and the three zero-click games are exactly the ones with the strongest P1 (1.0, 0.923, 1.0) -- but the artifact should have distinguished 'A1 checked and clean' from 'A1 had nothing to check'.

FINDING_1_positive_morphology_evidence.CORRECTION_to_the_review_frame_counts: The review quoted contiguity as 15/15, 17/17, 11/11, 13/13, 18/18. This recomputation counts one more frame per game (16, 18, 12, 14, 19) because it includes the final after-frame as well as every before-frame. Contiguity is 100% under either accounting, so the difference is bookkeeping, not disagreement.
FINDING_1_positive_morphology_evidence.CORRECTION_to_the_review_ka59: The review stated five of six bands satisfy ALL of the morphology tests, naming a 'constant colour-2 divider at row 62' for ka59. Recomputed, ka59's row 62 takes TWO distinct values over the trajectory, so the strict test FAILS and the strict count is 4 of 6, not 5. The substance survives and is arguably stronger than the review claimed: row 62 is a uniform colour-2 divider for all 11 within-level frames and changes at exactly one transition -- transition 10 -- which is the same transition at which the bar empties. The whole HUD strip redraws at the level boundary. Reported as M3b so both readings are visible; M3b is never substituted for M3.
FINDING_1_positive_morphology_evidence.claim_reviewed: the mask does not delete real playfield, and the reason is visible in the bands' SHAPE, not only in the absence of alarms
FINDING_1_positive_morphology_evidence.ls20_is_the_exception_and_the_review_cor: ls20 row 62 fails M1 (five colours), M2 and M3 outright. It is NOT a fill bar. That does not make it playfield -- M1-M3 are sufficient evidence of a bar, not necessary evidence of a HUD -- and ls20 has the strongest action-decoupling of any shipped band (P1 0.923 over 13 far opportunities AND P2 over three action ids). It reads as a different KIND of readout: eleven fixed positions, columns 13-23, that change no matter where or how you act. Notably it is also the one band the explorer's independent edge_bar detector does not corroborate, and the one flagged by FINDING_2 below. Three independent signals single out the same band, which is worth more than any one of them.

tests.M1: exactly two distinct colours ever appear in the band
tests.M2: the minority colour is a single contiguous run in EVERY frame (a bar)
tests.M3: the row/col immediately inside the band is constant (a divider)
tests.M4: the mover entity never occupies the band
tests.M5: the winning route never clicks inside the band
tests.M6: the band empties at the level boundary

FINDING_1_positive_morphology_evidence.verdict: SUBSTANTIALLY VERIFIED, with one band's divider claim corrected
FINDING_1_positive_morphology_evidence.why_these_are_stronger_than_the_original: M1-M3 are pure shape. They say nothing about actions, so they cannot be produced by whatever mechanism produces P1/P2's action-correlation signal. A band that is two-coloured, contiguous, divider-separated and empties on level-up is a progress bar by construction, not by inference from an alarm that stayed silent.

FINDING_2_ls20_masks_half_of_a_two_row_w.claim_reviewed: ls20 rows 61 and 62 are the same widget; the mask covers row 62 and leaves row 61 graded, and the detector could not have proposed row 61 even in principle
FINDING_2_ls20_masks_half_of_a_two_row_w.is_this_verdict_changing: No. A two-row mask would put 44 of the corpus's 2089 changed cells inside the mask -- overlap 0.021, still 24x under the shipped 0.5 swallow threshold -- so the band would clear the guard either way. This is recorded as a COMPLETENESS defect (the mask is half a widget) plus a DETECTOR LIMITATION (it cannot see the other half), not as a reason to withdraw the band.
FINDING_2_ls20_masks_half_of_a_two_row_w.mechanism: python/carnot/agentic/arc_entity_hud_perception.py:107 sets edge_margin=2, and lines 140/143 reject any candidate with 2 <= r < h-2. On a 64-row grid the only proposable rows are {0, 1, 62, 63}. Row 61 is structurally unreachable. The capture disclosed edge_margin=2 as 'an interior HUD is out of reach' (limitation 5) but not this consequence: any HUD widget deeper than two cells is silently HALF-masked, and the detector cannot report the shortfall because it never saw the other half.
FINDING_2_ls20_masks_half_of_a_two_row_w.verdict: VERIFIED EXACTLY, on both the data claim and the mechanism
FINDING_2_ls20_masks_half_of_a_two_row_w.what_would_settle_it: re-run detect_hud_registers with edge_margin=3 on ls20 alone and check whether row 61 is proposed and whether the two-row mask still clears both corpora. That is a THRESHOLD CHANGE, which this capture's no-tuning rule forbids doing silently, so it belongs in a follow-up with its own audit, not here.

FINDING_6_ka59_is_the_thinnest_stage_1_d.claim_reviewed: ka59's P1 discriminator failed and it ships on P2 alone, with only two qualifying action ids at n=4 each
FINDING_6_ka59_is_the_thinnest_stage_1_d.the_reviews_own_caveat_and_a_further_one: The review noted that a genuine 'ticks on the mere fact of acting' counter should fire under every action type, and ids 1 and 2 never changed the band. True -- but each of those ids was observed exactly ONCE, so 'never' rests on a single observation apiece and is weak evidence in both directions. The honest statement is that ka59's action-decoupling evidence is thin at n=11 transitions, not that it points the other way.
FINDING_6_ka59_is_the_thinnest_stage_1_d.what_actually_carries_this_band: morphology. ka59 row 63 is two-coloured, contiguous in 12/12 frames, has a uniform colour-2 divider at row 62 for every within-level frame, is never entered by the mover, changes in only six positions (58-63), and its fill runs 0,1,1,2,3,3,4,4,5,6,6 before resetting to 0 at level-up. That is a counter. Recorded plainly: the discriminators do not carry ka59; the shape does.

evidence_files.morphology_check.json: its output; two independent runs produced byte-identical output after stripping per-run durations

adversarial_review_2026_08_01.what_did_NOT_change: No mask was added, removed or altered. No threshold was touched. tn36 row 1 remains WITHHELD. The six default masks, their cell fractions, and every stage-1 and stage-2 decision are exactly as originally captured. This section adds evidence and names two defects; it changes no verdict.
adversarial_review_2026_08_01.what_prompted_this: An adversarial review of this capture accepted the two-stage gate but objected that every defence it offered was NEGATIVE -- three alarms that did not fire, plus two discriminators that measure how a band CORRELATES with actions. Nothing in the artifact said what the bands positively ARE. The review re-derived the bands' shape from environment_files and argued they are progress bars on morphology alone, which is evidence of a different kind and much harder to fake than an absent alarm. It also found two defects the capture had not reported. Everything below was INDEPENDENTLY recomputed by morphology_check.py (committed alongside) before being written here; two of the review's own figures did not reproduce as stated and are corrected rather than adopted.

which_defence_each_shipped_band_actually.ka59_row63: P2 only (P1 failed at 0.636) + full morphology under M3b
which_defence_each_shipped_band_actually.ls20_row62: P1 (0.923) + P2 (3 ids); FAILS morphology; masks half a two-row widget
which_defence_each_shipped_band_actually.reading: every shipped band has at least two independent legs, and no band rests on a single test. ls20 is the weakest on shape and the strongest on action-decoupling; ka59 is the reverse. That the two weakest-on-one-axis bands are strongest on the other is the reason both still ship.
which_defence_each_shipped_band_actually.s5i5_row63: P1 only (1.0, 13/13; P2 unavailable -- the whole route uses one action id) + full morphology

detector_comparison_vs_explorer_edge_bar.band_definition: a row/col the explorer covers to >=90%; the strict all-cells test misreported tn36's 61-of-64 bar as no band at all

determinism_note: The route replay, the detectors and the audit are deterministic functions of the offline environment_files, so random_seed is recorded for provenance rather than because a sampler consumed it -- stating that plainly is better than implying a seed swept a distribution it never touched. The one genuinely seeded component is the SECOND corpus, collect_transitions(n=60, seed=0); seed 0 is not this artifact's seed but the one REQ-ARC-WMTE-6015's table was measured at, chosen so the comparison to that table is meaningful. Repeatability is measured, not asserted -- see determinism_recheck.

determinism_recheck.what_this_does_not_test: Both runs used the same checkout, the same environment_files and any learned verifier checkpoints already on disk. It is a same-machine repeatability check, not an independent reproduction.
determinism_recheck.what_this_tests: Two independent full runs of capture.py, each re-solving every game through solve_adaptered and re-cutting its window. Identical detected bands mean the route, the window and the detector are all reproducible -- the thing a third party needs in order to re-derive these masks rather than take them on trust.

duration_s_note: Sum of the per-game capture durations recorded in per_game.json plus the cross-corpus check's own duration. Excludes interpreter startup and artifact assembly.
inference_substrate_note: CPU-only. The offline arcade is stepped through each game's own winning route to rebuild the induction window (build_progress_window), and separately with random salience-ordered actions (collect_transitions) for the second corpus. Pure-numpy detectors (detect_hud_registers, detect_mover) and the shipped swallow guard then run over the resulting (grid, action, grid) transitions. NO LLM is loaded, no GGUF is invoked, no llama-server is contacted, no GPU is used, and none of the 116 A/B induced engines is imported or executed.
limitations: The masks are derived from ONE route per game -- the offline arcade's own winning route to L1 -- plus one 60-action random corpus. A band that only reveals itself as playfield on a third corpus is invisible to this audit, and that error direction is not symmetric: a missed playfield alarm ships an over-mask.

Six of the 20 windows are shorter than 10 transitions (lp85 5, cd82 5, tn36 7, su15 7, lf52 8, sb26 9). On those the stage-1 statistics rest on single-digit denominators, so a passing discriminator is weak evidence even when its rate is 1.0.

A2 keys on the mover's COLOR occupying the band, not a tracked instance, so a HUD sharing the player's palette trips it and the band is excluded. That is a deliberate under-mask, chosen because the opposite error is the catastrophic one. detect_mover returned None on several games, so A2 was simply unavailable there.

P1 falls back to the mover's centroid as 'where the agent acted' for directional actions -- a proxy for an action that has no coordinate. On lp85 the recorded action id was 0 with no data and no mover, so no discriminator was available at all and the band was refused rather than guessed at.
detect_hud_registers only ever proposes bands within edge_margin=2. A status readout drawn in the grid's interior is outside this detector's reach by construction.
This capture does NOT re-score the A/B and makes no claim about change_fidelity. It produces masks and the evidence that they may be used.

ADDED 2026-08-01 after adversarial review: ls20's mask covers row 62 but rows 61 and 62 are byte-identical in 14/14 frames with identical change masks in 13/13 transitions -- the mask is half a two-row widget. detect_hud_registers(edge_margin=2) cannot propose row 61 on a 64-row grid, so any HUD widget deeper than two cells is silently half-masked and the detector cannot report the shortfall. Not verdict-changing (a two-row mask overlaps only 0.021 of changed cells, well under the 0.5 swallow threshold) but the mask is incomplete.

ADDED 2026-08-01 after adversarial review: alarm A1 (the winning route never clicks inside the band) is VACUOUS on ar25, ls20 and tu93, whose routes contain no click actions at all. Three of the six reported A1 passes carry no information. A1 should be three-valued (clean / alarm / unavailable) rather than a bool.

ADDED 2026-08-01 after adversarial review: ka59 is the only shipped band whose P1 discriminator FAILED (0.636 < 0.7); it ships on P2 alone, with two qualifying action ids at n=4 each, out of 11 transitions total. Its morphology is unambiguous (two-colour contiguous counter, six changing positions, resets at level-up), so the band is defensible -- but on shape, not on the discriminators the capture cited.

ADDED 2026-08-01 after adversarial review: ls20 row 62 FAILS the progress-bar morphology tests outright (five colours, no contiguous run, no constant divider). It is still strongly action-decoupled (P1 0.923, P2 over three action ids) and is best described as a non-bar readout, but the shipped mask set is not homogeneous and this artifact originally presented it as though it were.

masks_written.consumption_note: Each file gives (logical_shape, hud_rows, hud_cols) -- a lossless encoding of the boolean mask, since a band is a whole row or column. A re-score materialises it with two numpy assignments and passes it to arc_executable_world_model.apply_hud_mask on BOTH sides of the comparison. An EMPTY mask is a refusal, not an absence: apply nothing and record mask_status. conditionally_clean_bands are NOT in hud_rows/hud_cols and require a deliberate opt-in.

no_solve_is_claimed_note: No ARC level is solved, reproduced or claimed here. The winning routes replayed to build the windows are already-banked registry routes used purely as a transition source; solve_provenance is therefore not declared, because declaring one would assert a solve this artifact does not make.

stage_1_single_corpus.A1_solution_acts_in_band: the offline arcade's own winning route clicks inside the band => the band is interactive playfield
stage_1_single_corpus.A2_mover_occupies_band: the detected PLAYER entity's color occupies band cells in some observed frame => the band is somewhere the game is played
stage_1_single_corpus.A3_swallow_guard: REQ-ARC-WMTE-6015's shipped hud_mask_swallow_check / hud_mask_swallow_clean on the band-alone mask; anything that is not the affirmative 'ok' verdict is a refusal, including the unmeasurable ones
stage_1_single_corpus.P1_far_action_decoupling: the band changes even when the action was >= 4 cells away along the band's axis, at a rate >= 0.7 over >= 3 far opportunities
stage_1_single_corpus.P2_action_type_decoupling: >= 2 distinct action ids each change the band on >= 50% of their frame-changing transitions
stage_1_single_corpus.corpus: the game's own winning route to L1 (window + full trajectory)
stage_1_single_corpus.threshold_provenance: 0.7 is the detector's own pos_independent_min and 0.5 is its own mixed_changed_min, reused rather than chosen fresh so the audit adds no new tunable. 4 cells is edge_margin=2 plus a two-cell buffer, so a FAR action provably did not land on or beside the band.

corpus.why_this_scope: REQ-ARC-WMTE-6019 records that REQ-ARC-WMTE-6015's over-masking table was measured at n=60, seed=0, and that n=60 is a strict prefix of n=120 under the same seed. Matching the scope is what makes a comparison to that table meaningful rather than a fresh unrelated measurement.

stage_2_second_corpus.gate: a band reaches hud_rows/hud_cols only if affirmatively clean on BOTH corpora; otherwise it is moved to conditionally_clean_bands in the mask file, which is NOT part of the mask a consumer materialises
stage_2_second_corpus.refusal_classes_are_not_the_same_claim: 'mask_overlaps_majority_of_changed_cells' (su15) is MEASURED evidence the mask covers what changes. 'no_changed_cells_outside_mask_cannot_distinguish' (lf52, tn36) is the shipped guard's explicitly UNMEASURABLE verdict -- the corpus cannot tell an honest counter from a mask that covers the game. Both are refusals under hud_mask_swallow_clean's default-refuse contract, and they are reported separately because they are different facts and an operator acts on them differently.
stage_2_second_corpus.why: Stage 1 accepted a band on lf52 and su15 -- the exact two games REQ-ARC-WMTE-6015 documents as over-masking cases. A single-corpus accept is therefore not enough to ship a mask, because REQ-ARC-WMTE-6017 already recorded that lf52's verdict FLIPS between a random-action corpus (refused) and a live episode (applied).

over_masking_audit.the_finding_that_survives_regardless_of_: The two detectors agree on the band on 8 of 20 games (bp35, ka59, lf52, lp85, s5i5, su15, tn36, tu93) -- including tn36, where both independently pick row 1, the exact row the induced engines model. Two unrelated methods converging on the same band is stronger evidence that it is chrome than either alone. They differ in BOTH directions elsewhere: 7 games where only the explorer proposes a band (cd82, g50t, m0r0, re86, sc25, tr87, wa30) and 2 where only this capture does (cn04, ls20). Those directions are not equivalent: a band only this detector proposes is a candidate over-mask the shipped path never risked, while a band only the explorer proposes is coverage this transition-derived path does not reproduce. Both facts are properties of the detectors and hold whichever mask is used.
over_masking_audit.why_this_is_the_first_deliverable: If a flagged band is really playfield, masking deletes real dynamics: every engine's score IMPROVES while it models LESS, and nothing in the numbers says so. logical_hud_mask's own docstring names the asymmetry -- 'over-masking destroys CORRECTNESS while under-masking only costs efficiency' -- so the audit GATES the mask instead of annotating it.

preconditions_checked.detail: edge_bar_hud_mask importable, for the same-band comparison
CPU-only: offline arcade env-stepping plus numpy detectors

provenance.code_sha256_format: bare hex digest, no 'sha256:' prefix -- the format scripts/artifact_freshness_lint.py compares against

the_sharp_test.a_correction_this_artifact_makes_to_itse: An earlier build of this artifact asserted that the explorer proposes NOTHING on tn36. That was false and came from summarising the explorer's mask by strictly-complete rows only: its tn36 mask covers row 1 columns 1..61, a band by any reading, which an `.all()` test reports as no rows at all. The comparison now counts a row/col as a band at >=90% coverage AND reports raw cell-level overlap, so the claim does not depend on that threshold. Recorded rather than silently fixed, because the false version made this capture look more novel than it is.
the_sharp_test.principle: Reported either way. A MISS would have been a finding about the detector, not a reason to hand-add the band; a HIT that fails the second corpus is a finding about the mask, not a reason to relax the gate.
the_sharp_test.question: tn36's induced goal predicate is literally the progress bar -- `np.all(grid[1, 1:62] == 3)`, ROW 1, inside the edge band. If detect_hud_registers misses row 1, the whole hypothesis fails at step one.
the_sharp_test.the_honest_reading: The detector PASSES the sharp test: row 1 is found on the shipped defaults, changed_fraction 1.0, and it is the exact row the engines model. The explorer's own frame-space edge_bar detector INDEPENDENTLY masks the same row 1 (61 of its 64 cells, cell-level Jaccard 0.953) -- two unrelated detectors agreeing on the band, which is stronger evidence that row 1 is chrome than either alone. What this path adds is not a band the explorer missed but a RECONSTRUCTION route: the band comes from transitions in LOGICAL coordinates, so it exists where the A/B said a mask was 'not reconstructible from this run's evidence'. But it does NOT reach the default mask: on the random-action corpus it shows the same 1.0000 overlap / 60 changing -> 0 surviving signature as lf52, the documented over-masking case. Detection succeeded; licensing failed. The consequence is stated rather than softened -- this capture does NOT deliver a default mask that fixes the six perfect-1.0 tn36 bar-ticker candidates.

title: Per-game LOGICAL HUD-band capture for the object-perception A/B roster, gated by a two-corpus over-masking audit

upstream_module_drift_note_2026_08_01.how_a_reader_should_treat_it: as a provenance-drift note, not a staleness warning. Neither of these artifacts is registered in ops/analyzer_artifact_index.json, so scripts/artifact_freshness_lint.py does not cover them; that is a real coverage gap and this note is the manual substitute for it.
upstream_module_drift_note_2026_08_01.what: python/carnot/agentic/arc_executable_world_model.py changed after this run, in a concurrent session's commit b6787cb603. This artifact's provenance still pins the sha256 the run actually used (94fd91a4...), which is correct and is deliberately NOT updated -- provenance records what produced the numbers, not what is on disk today.
upstream_module_drift_note_2026_08_01.why_not: the change adds `_reject_inert_engines()` and one opt-in branch inside `LocalGGUFProposer`'s induce path, gated on CARNOT_ARC_INDUCE_REJECT_INERT which defaults OFF. It touches neither `change_fidelity`, nor `hud_mask_swallow_check`, nor `logical_hud_mask` -- the three functions every figure in this artifact depends on. With the flag unset the module is behaviourally identical on this path.

verifier_is_oracle_not_applicable_note: This artifact makes no verifier-value, moat or efficiency claim -- it emits no score and reranks nothing. It is perception capture, so the circularity question does not arise.
what_this_delivers: 6 of 20 roster games carry a default logical HUD mask that is affirmatively clean on BOTH the winning-route corpus and the random-action corpus, written to masks/*.json in a form a re-score materialises with two numpy assignments. Every other game ships an EMPTY mask, which is a refusal with a recorded reason, not an absence.
what_this_does_not_deliver: It does not re-score the A/B, and it does not fix the tn36 degeneracy: tn36 row 1 is detected and then withheld. Any claim that masking changes change_fidelity, or that the six perfect-1.0 candidates stop being perfect, requires a separate measurement that has not been run.
